items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: Ben Webster wanted to know if I'd like to go into the Famous Door, he was going in to the Famous Door with a band

ctx.x: Another aside -- Clyde Hart died while we were on that engagement with the Three Deuces, and he had tuberculosis, which I didn't know. But he was very sick all the time he was playing, and I helped put him in a cab one morning after we got through playing, and he said, 'No, I'll get uptown all right, somebody is meeting me.' And I never saw him again -- he died during the night.

Now to a wonderful era in my life, we'll get to Ben now, Ben Webster. Just a few weeks after being at the Deuces with Don Byas, Ben Webster wanted to know if I'd like to go into the Famous Door, he was going in to the Famous Door with a band, and I don't know how to explain this -- but he had some arrangements. The Famous Door wanted to be different from the other clubs on the Street, there was so much bop going on and everything was happening, bop was being flown then.
